slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌

第九章归人
三天后，老周果然在街角等着。
苏尘走过去的时候，他正低着头翻一本破旧的《麻衣相法》，面前的签筒里插着几支竹签，看着跟平时没什么两样。苏尘在摊前坐下，把一枚玄铢放在桌上。
“先生，算个命。“
老周抬起头，眯眼笑了笑，收起那枚玄铢，压低声音道：“孙石匠和马木匠都应了。工钱按您说的双倍，他们二话没说就点了头。孙石匠说随时能动，马木匠那边得把手头一个零活收个尾，后天就能来。“
苏尘点了点头。跟他预想的差不多。
“材料呢？“
“青砖和石灰我托人问了，城南的窑厂有货，价格公道。木料要从城外的一个老木场进，那老板跟我熟，能给个实在价。您要是定下来了，我三天之内把料备齐。“
苏尘在心里算了算。青砖、石灰、木料、瓦片，再加上石匠和木匠的工钱，这笔开销不小。他从钱袋里摸出一枚中品玄铢，放在桌上，用手掌压住。
“这是定金。料钱和工钱从这里面出，不够再跟我说。“
老周看了一眼那枚中品玄铢，眼神微微一动。一枚中品玄铢抵一百枚下品，在这朔州城够一户普通人家过上大半年了。他没有多说什么，只是重重地点了点头，不动声色地把玄铢收进袖中。
“少主放心，账目我会一笔一笔记清楚。“
“后天开工。我先去马场等着，你们到了直接开始。先砌围墙，再修正屋，密室最后挖。“
“明白。“
苏尘站起身，拍了拍衣摆上的灰，头也不回地走了。他没有直接出城，而是先绕到城南的窑厂看了一眼。窑厂门口堆着一排一排的青砖，颜色均匀，敲起来声音清脆，品质不错。他又绕到西市，找到老周说的那家木料场，在门口站了一会儿，看了一会儿进出的木材。木料大多是新伐的，树皮还没剥干净，堆在院子里散发着一股松脂的气味。他注意到角落里堆着几根老料，表面已经风干发暗，用手指敲了敲，声音沉实，是好料。他记下了那几根老料的位置，转身走了。
材料和工匠都定了，接下来就看施工了。
两天后，马场准时动了工。
孙石匠带着两个儿子来的。大的约莫十七八岁，长得敦实，一双大手满是老茧，一看就是从小跟着干活的；小的才十三四，瘦一些，但眼神活泛，搬砖和灰手脚麻利。马木匠带了五个徒弟，扛着锯子刨子锤子，一行七八个人浩浩荡荡地来了。这些人往院子里一站，原本空旷破败的场地一下子显得拥挤起来，荒草被踩平了一大片，原本冷清的马场第一次有了人声和工具敲击的声响。
苏尘站在院子中央，把图纸在地上铺开。
说是图纸，其实就是他自己画的几张简图——围墙的尺寸、正屋的结构、密室的位置和深度、通风暗道的走向。线条简陋，但尺寸标得清清楚楚，关键位置都用朱砂点了标记。前世在玄镜司督造过不少密所，对建筑布局的造诣还在脑子里，虽然画工粗糙，但该有的细节一个没落下。

孙石匠蹲下来看了半天，抬头看了苏尘一眼。
“小公子，这密室……挖这么深？“
“一丈深。墙砌青砖，顶要横梁加固。“
孙石匠捻了捻手指，没再问。他干了大半辈子石匠活，知道什么该问什么不该问。这个小公子出手大方，给钱爽快，图的肯定不是养马那么简单。但对方不说，他也不问。
马木匠倒是话多一些，绕着正屋走了一圈，又爬上断墙看了看屋顶的结构，下来拍了拍手上的灰。
“正屋的梁得换，原来的都朽了。我手头有几根好木料，从南边带上来的，放了大半年，干透了，用在这正合适。“
“你看着办。“苏尘说，“用料要好，工期要快。“
“工期的话，围墙快些，十来天就能立起来。正屋翻修慢一些，得先把旧料拆干净，新料要现加工，至少半个月。至于地下那间——“马木匠看了一眼孙石匠，“那是老孙的活，我一个木匠搭把手可以，主要还得他来。“
孙石匠在旁边闷声回了一句：“地下那个快不了。挖坑容易，砌墙加固得慢慢来，急不得。“
“工人在城墙根搭了棚子住，离这儿好几里路。小公子，您看能不能在院子里搭个临时的棚屋？省得每天来回跑，耽误工夫。“
苏尘想了想，点头应了。人住在这里，日夜都有人盯着，安全性反而更高。于是一天之内，马场的空地上就搭起了两间简易的棚屋，一间住人，一间堆料。石匠和木匠分了工，各干各的。围墙最先动工，孙石匠带着两个儿子在旧墙基上挖槽、砌砖。他们干活确实利落，配合默契，话也不多。苏尘站在旁边看了一会儿，发现孙石匠每砌几层就要拉一根线量一量水平，一丝不苟。他心里踏实了些。正屋的翻修紧随其后，马木匠带着徒弟把朽坏的梁拆下来，换上新的，榫头严丝合缝，不用铁钉，全是传统手艺。
开工的头几天，苏尘几乎天天都去。有时候是早上到，站在院子里看一会儿，跟孙石匠或者马木匠说几句话；有时候是下午去，在工地边上蹲着，看工人砌砖、上梁，偶尔指出一两句尺寸上的偏差。他一个十岁的孩子站在一群大人中间，说话做事却一点不像个孩子。孙石匠私下跟儿子说过一次：“这小公子不简单，你们干活仔细些，别让人挑出错来。“
围墙砌了小半人高的时候，苏尘特意让木匠在正屋的地面上留了一个不大的开口——以后密室挖出来的土方，要从这个口子运出去，不能堆在院子里让人看见。马木匠虽然不明白为什么要留这个口，但也没多问，照做了。苏尘对他的不多问很满意。第三天傍晚，苏尘到马场的时候，正赶上孙石匠的小儿子在墙根下和泥，和得太稀了，砌上去砖直往下滑。孙石匠走过来看了一眼，没骂人，只是蹲下来重新和了一摊，让小儿子在旁边看着。小儿子红着脸，一声不吭地学着。苏尘站在不远处看着这一幕，觉得这对父子还算靠谱。
日子一天天过去。马场的围墙一天比一天高，正屋的屋顶重新铺了瓦，连那几间塌了的马厩也重新立了起来。每天傍晚他离开的时候，回头看一眼，都能看到和早上来的时候不一样的变化。这种看得见的进展让人安心——脚下的地在变，头顶的瓦在变，围起来的院子一天比一天像样。
苏尘的生活也开始有了规律——早上在府里待着，吃过午饭就出城去马场看看，傍晚回来，晚上在自己的房间里练纳气法。柳含烟问了几次，他说去马场看施工，她也没多管，只说别耽误了吃饭。
第九章归人
苏尘的修为在缓慢但稳定地增长。纳气法虽然效率低，但日日不间断地练，总归是有效果的。他能感觉到丹田里的那缕气感越来越凝实，从最初的一根头发丝那么细，到现在已经有了一根线那么粗。虽然离突破还远得很——淬体境入境到中期，按他这个速度至少还要一年——但他不着急。底子打得越扎实，后面的路走得越稳。

Chapter 9 Returning
Three days later, Lao Zhou was waiting at the street corner.
When Su Chen walked over, he was looking down and flipping through a shabby "Ma Yi Xiangfa". There were a few bamboo sticks inserted in the bamboo stick in front of him, which looked the same as usual. Su Chen sat down in front of the stall and placed a xuan baht on the table.
"Sir, tell me your fortune."
Lao Zhou raised his head, squinted his eyes and smiled, put away the black baht, and lowered his voice and said: "Shijiang Sun and Carpenter Ma are both ready. The wages will be doubled as you said. They nodded without saying a word. Shijiang Sun said they can move at any time, but Carpenter Ma has to finish the odd job and he can come the day after tomorrow."
Su Chen nodded. Pretty much what he expected.
"Where are the materials?"
"I asked someone about the green bricks and lime. The kiln factory in the south of the city has the goods and the price is fair. The wood needs to be imported from an old lumberyard outside the city. The boss is familiar with me and can give a real price. If you decide, I will have the materials ready within three days."
Su Chen calculated in his mind. Bricks, lime, wood, tiles, plus the labor of masons and carpenters, this expense is not small. He took out a medium-grade black baht from his wallet, placed it on the table, and pressed it with his palm.
"This is the deposit. The materials and labor will come from here. If it's not enough, don't tell me."
Lao Zhou glanced at the middle-grade Xuan Baht and his eyes moved slightly. One medium-grade black baht is worth a hundred low-grade coins, which is enough for an ordinary family to live for more than half a year in Shuozhou City. He didn't say anything more, just nodded solemnly and put the Xuan Bah into his sleeve calmly.
"Don't worry, young master, I will write down the accounts clearly one by one."
"The work will start the day after tomorrow. I'll wait at the racecourse first, and we'll start right away when you arrive. First build the wall, then repair the house, and finally dig the secret room."
"Understood."
Su Chen stood up, patted the dust on his clothes, and left without looking back. He did not leave the city directly, but first went around to the kiln factory in the south of the city to take a look. There are rows of green bricks piled up at the entrance of the kiln. They are uniform in color, have a crisp sound when knocked, and are of good quality. He went around to the West Market and found the lumberyard that Lao Zhou had mentioned. He stood at the door for a while and looked at the lumber coming in and out. Most of the wood was newly cut, and the bark had not yet been peeled off. It smelled like pine resin when piled in the yard. He noticed that there were several old materials piled up in the corner. The surface had been dried and darkened. He tapped them with his fingers. The sound was solid, indicating that they were good materials. He noted the location of the old materials, turned around and left.
The materials and craftsmen have been decided, and the next step is construction.
Two days later, construction on the racecourse started on time.
Sun Shijiang came with his two sons. The eldest one is about seventeen or eighteen years old, he is stocky, and his big hands are covered with calluses. It can be seen that he has been working since he was a child. The younger one is only thirteen or fourteen, thinner, but has lively eyes, and his hands and feet are quick to move bricks and dust. Carpenter Ma brought five apprentices, carrying saws, planes, and hammers, and a group of seven or eight people came in force. As soon as these people stood in the yard, the originally empty and dilapidated venue suddenly became crowded. A large area of ​​grass was trampled down. For the first time, the originally deserted racecourse heard the sounds of people and the hammering of tools.
Su Chen stood in the middle of the yard and spread the drawings on the ground.
They are called drawings, but they are actually a few simple drawings he drew himself - the size of the wall, the structure of the main house, the location and depth of the secret room, and the direction of the ventilation passage. The lines are simple, but the dimensions are clearly marked, and key positions are marked with cinnabar dots. In his previous life, he had supervised the construction of many secret places in the Xuanjing Division, and his knowledge of architectural layouts was still in his mind. Although his painting skills were rough, not a single detail was missing.
Sun Shijiang knelt down and looked for a long time, then raised his head and glanced at Su Chen.
"Young Master, is this secret room... dug so deep?"
"One foot deep. The walls are built with blue bricks and the tops are reinforced with beams."
Shijiang Sun twirled his fingers and didn't ask any more questions. He had been working as a mason for most of his life and knew what to ask and what not to ask. This young man is generous with his money and gives money readily. He is definitely not trying to support his family.Horses are so simple. But the other party didn't tell him, and he didn't ask.
Carpenter Ma was more talkative. He walked around the main house, climbed up the broken wall and looked at the structure of the roof, then came down and patted the dust off his hands.
"The beams in the main house need to be replaced. The original ones are all rotten. I have some good wood on hand. I brought it from the south. It has been stored for more than half a year and has dried thoroughly. It is suitable for use here."
"It's up to you." Su Chen said, "The materials should be good and the construction period should be fast."
"In terms of construction time, the wall should be faster. It can be erected in about ten days. The renovation of the main house is slower. The old materials must be removed first and the new materials must be processed on-site, which will take at least half a month. As for the underground room -" Carpenter Ma glanced at Mason Sun, "That is Lao Sun's job. I and my carpenter can help, but he is the main one."
Stonemason Sun replied in a muffled voice next to him: "The underground one won't be fast. It's easy to dig a hole, but you have to build and reinforce the wall slowly. There's no rush."
"The workers have built a shack to live at the base of the city wall, several miles away from here. Young Master, do you think you can build a temporary shack in the yard? This will save you the time of running back and forth every day."
Su Chen thought for a while and nodded in agreement. People living here will be watched day and night, which makes it safer. So within one day, two simple shacks were erected on the open space of the racecourse, one for people to live in and one for stacking materials. The masons and carpenters divided the work and each did his own thing. The construction of the wall started first. Mason Sun and his two sons dug trenches and laid bricks on the foundation of the old wall. They work really neatly, work well together, and don't talk much. Su Chen stood aside and watched for a while, and found that Mason Sun would pull a thread to measure the level every few layers he built, and he was meticulous. He felt more at ease. The renovation of the main house followed closely. Carpenter Ma and his apprentices removed the decayed beams and replaced them with new ones. The tenons fit tightly without nails, all using traditional craftsmanship.
In the first few days of construction, Su Chen went there almost every day. Sometimes I arrive in the morning, stand in the yard and watch for a while, and say a few words to Mason Sun or Carpenter Ma; sometimes I go there in the afternoon, squatting at the edge of the construction site, watching the workers laying bricks and installing beams, and occasionally pointing out one or two deviations in size. He was a ten-year-old child standing among a group of adults, but he didn't act like a child at all. Sun Shijiang once said to his son in private: "This young master is not simple. You should work carefully and don't let others find mistakes."
When the wall was built to be less than half a person's height, Su Chen specially asked the carpenter to leave a small opening on the ground of the main house - the earth excavated from the secret room would be transported out through this opening and could not be piled in the yard for people to see. Although Carpenter Ma didn't understand why he wanted to leave this mouth open, he didn't ask any more questions and did as he was told. Su Chen was very satisfied with his lack of questions. On the evening of the third day, when Su Chen arrived at the racecourse, he caught up with Sun Shijiang's youngest son kneading mud under the base of the wall. The mud was too thin and the bricks slid down when they were put in place. Sun Shijiang came over and took a look. He didn't curse, but squatted down and made peace again, letting his youngest son watch. The younger son blushed and imitated without saying a word. Su Chen stood not far away and watched this scene, feeling that the father and son were quite reliable.
The days passed. The walls of the racecourse are getting taller day by day, the roof of the main house has been re-tiled, and even the collapsed stables have been re-erected. Every evening when he left, he looked back and saw the changes that were different from when he came in the morning. This kind of visible progress is reassuring - the ground beneath our feet is changing, the tiles above our heads are changing, and the fenced-in yard is getting better and better day by day.
Su Chen's life also began to have a routine - he stayed at the house in the morning, went out to the city to visit the racecourse after lunch, came back in the evening, and practiced the Qi method in his room at night. Liu Hanyan asked several times. He said he went to the racecourse to see the construction, but she didn't pay much attention. She just said don't delay eating.
Chapter 9 Returning
Su Chen's cultivation level was growing slowly but steadily. Although the Naqi method is inefficient, it works continuously every dayPractice will always be effective. He could feel the qi in his Dantian becoming more and more solid, from being as thin as a hair to now being as thick as a thread. Although he was still far from a breakthrough—it would take at least a year to reach the middle stage of the Body Tempering Realm at his rate—but he was not in a hurry. The more solid the foundation is, the more stable the road ahead will be.
